[1/2] Collapse the portfolio header and filter chrome: one-line intro, one search/sort row, count-free discipline chips, no topic chip row, single result count, count-free atlas status

impact_assessment.why: The portfolio stacked five control rows and repeated the repository total four times, burying the cards
impact_assessment.benefits: Cards start sooner; one count per surface; less DOM, CSS and JS to maintain
impact_assessment.risks: contract: chip badges, topic row and count-bearing status text removed; dependency: none; concurrency: one service-worker cache version bump; state: topic deep links and the topic URL parameter still work
impact_assessment.mitigation: Update the Python and Node tests with the markup, keep topic filtering by URL and search, bump the service-worker version, and run every gate

checkpoints.description: [2/2] Portfolio trimmed: one-line intro, search/sort row, six count-free discipline chips, no topic row, one result count, count-free atlas status, service worker v2; ADR-026; 78 Python tests, 52 atlas, 58 verifier and 32 project assertions, 4/4 gates pass; checklists: passed
Task 'portfolio-trim' completed successfully.

[1/4] Put topic chips back inside the discipline row (count-free), add a dossier logo slot and a screenshot gallery fed by a per-repository media manifest that records the commit and date of every capture

impact_assessment.why: The single discipline row lost topic discovery, and dossiers have no logo or screenshot surface even though captures will soon exist
impact_assessment.benefits: One chip row covers discipline and topics; dossiers can show a real logo and commit-stamped screenshots without a build step
impact_assessment.risks: contract: docs/media/<Repo>.json schema and dossier markup; dependency: browser fetch only; concurrency: none; state: media manifests and images, no credentials
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure normalization helpers with Node tests, safe relative media paths only, hidden sections until media exists, Python and Node parity tests

checkpoints.description: [2/4] Topic chips are back inside the discipline row: quiet dashed pills, no counts, top 12 by usage, separator; filtering and URL state unchanged; 79 Python tests, 52 atlas assertions pass; checklists: passed

[3/4] Dossier logo slot with monogram fallback and a screenshot gallery; docs/media/<Name>.json schema validated (media/ paths, 7-40 hex commit, real date, 12 cap); commit links to GitHub; no capture exists yet so both slots stay hidden; 57 project assertions pass; checklists: passed

[4/4] docs/media/README.md records the manifest schema and capture workflow; README tree and dossier paragraph updated; ADR-027; service worker v3; 79 Python tests, 58 verifier, 52 atlas and 57 project assertions, 4/4 gates pass; checklists: passed
Task 'media-groundwork' completed successfully.
[1/3] Name each repository's Aegean license family on cards and dossiers; add Reforge to the snapshot, JSON-LD, README, cards, tests and license ledger after it was published on GitHub

impact_assessment.why: Every card said Custom license despite AL/AGL/ASL files, and the site claimed 34 projects while GitHub served 35
impact_assessment.benefits: Visitors see the license that binds them; catalogue, JSON-LD, README and snapshot agree on 35 repos
impact_assessment.risks: contract: data-license and license labels change; dependency: none; concurrency: live GitHub sync must not overwrite the family; state: REPO_LICENSES ledger must be maintained
impact_assessment.mitigation: license_family survives normalizeRepo, Python derives expectations from the same ledger, Node pins the mapping
